## The idea

This capstone turns one complete monophonic source into structured score data.
Choose thirty-two to sixty-four bars from the shortlist built in Lesson 42.
The piece needs enough length to contain several phrases, a high point, repeated
material, and at least one passage that resists immediate transcription.
Complete the four-pass pipeline in
[Lesson 43](../09-transcription/43-four-pass-pipeline.qmd) and the debugging
checks in [Lesson 46](../09-transcription/46-debug-transcription-like-software.qmd)
on a short excerpt before committing to the whole source.

The deliverable has two layers. The first is a faithful event list containing
pitch, start, duration, articulation, dynamics, and phrase information. The
second is an expressive renderer. Measure references and uncertainty markers
stay attached to the data so every claim can be traced back to the score or
recording.

Avoid choosing a piece because its first four bars are easy. Inspect the whole
range, fastest rhythm, accidentals, ornaments, and source quality. A clean
thirty-two-bar melody produces a better capstone than a famous theme whose
recording hides half its attacks.

## Run this

The block is a two-bar model of the final representation. Starts are global,
while measure and phrase fields support review. The renderer derives release
and amplitude from the score rather than rewriting notes.

```{.ruby audio=""}
use_bpm 74
use_synth :piano

score = [
  {measure: 1, phrase: :a, note: :c4, start: 0.0, duration: 1.0, amp: 0.62, articulation: :legato},
  {measure: 1, phrase: :a, note: :d4, start: 1.0, duration: 1.0, amp: 0.68, articulation: :legato},
  {measure: 1, phrase: :a, note: :e4, start: 2.0, duration: 2.0, amp: 0.78, articulation: :accent},
  {measure: 2, phrase: :a, note: :g4, start: 4.0, duration: 1.0, amp: 0.86, articulation: :accent},
  {measure: 2, phrase: :a, note: :e4, start: 5.0, duration: 1.0, amp: 0.72, articulation: :detached},
  {measure: 2, phrase: :a, note: :d4, start: 6.0, duration: 1.0, amp: 0.66, articulation: :legato},
  {measure: 2, phrase: :a, note: :c4, start: 7.0, duration: 1.0, amp: 0.58, articulation: :legato}
]

define :play_events do |events|
  cursor = 0.0
  events.each do |event|
    sleep event[:start] - cursor
    release_ratio = event[:articulation] == :detached ? 0.48 : 0.9
    accent_gain = event[:articulation] == :accent ? 0.12 : 0.0
    play event[:note],
      release: event[:duration] * release_ratio,
      amp: event[:amp] + accent_gain
    cursor = event[:start]
  end
  sleep events.last[:duration]
end

play_events score
```

The phrase grows toward G4, then recedes. The detached E creates one short gap
without changing the event's notated duration.

## Change one thing

1. Set every amp to 0.7. The contour remains, while the phrase loses its dynamic
   high point. Restore the data and decide whether dynamics belong to the source
   or your rendering.
2. Change the G articulation from :accent to :legato. The highest note remains
   structurally important but receives less attack emphasis. Compare pitch
   climax with performance emphasis.
3. Add source_time or source_page to every event, plus a REVIEW field on one
   uncertain note. Print those fields before playback. The sound stays fixed,
   while the audit trail becomes inspectable.

## Why it works

One event schema allows separate tools to agree. Bar-total checks use start and
duration. Range checks use note. The renderer uses articulation and amp.
Provenance tools use measure and source location. No helper needs to parse a
special representation for one phrase.

Absolute starts expose gaps and overlaps. Measure numbers preserve the source's
coordinate system. Phrase labels reveal form without copying events into
section-specific arrays. If a repeated phrase varies on its return, keep the
new events and label the relationship rather than aliasing data that is no
longer identical.

The capstone is complete only after review at several scales. Validate each bar,
loop each phrase, compare the whole contour, then audition the expressive
rendering from beginning to end. Automated Ruby checks cannot confirm the
source match or the intended sound, so keep the file at draft until a human
works through it in Sonic Pi.

## Take it further

Complete the thirty-two-to-sixty-four-bar transcription. Include a source
record, bar-by-bar validation report, global range, phrase labels, articulation,
dynamics, and a list of every uncertain passage with source coordinates.
Render the melody twice: score-strict and expressive. The structural constraint
is one score array feeding both renderers. The target sound is a faithful
monophonic performance whose phrase high points and cadences remain audible
without changing any pitch or duration between versions.
